page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at speeds up to 4.5 GHz, providing 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Cache architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory allocation sits at 64.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 1888 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates under Microsoft Hyper-V with support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and hardware encryption routines via AES and VAES.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-threaded compute and compression throughput. The instance achieves top-decile performance in stress-ng single-core tests and single-threaded gzip compression at 40.09 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector extension workloads show strong results, evidenced by a 40280.82 PassMark encryption score and elevated extended instructions metrics. High sustained clock frequencies also drive top-tier text generation on small language models (404.59 tokens/sec). Conversely, multi-core stress testing and database-oriented benchmarks, such as Redis SET operations at 53.41 million operations per second, place squarely in the median 50% band.

The 2:1 memory-to-core allocation provides an efficient resource profile for computationally intensive workloads that do not demand extensive in-memory footprints. Paired with 1888 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage, the configuration reduces cost overhead compared to standard 4 GB-per-vCPU profiles. D32alds_v7 is well aligned with CI/CD build farms, batch compression pipelines, edge web-tier delivery, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks relying on fast scratch disk access.
description: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v7 is an x86_64 instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 1888 GB local NVMe SSD without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks reveal top-tier single-thread performance, leading scores in gzip compression and small-model LLM text generation, alongside strong PassMark CPU encryption metrics. Multi-threaded throughput and Redis transaction rates remain in the median distribution. With a lower memory-per-core ratio and rapid local NVMe disk, this configuration minimizes excess memory expenditure while providing dense compute capability. It is effectively suited for continuous integration build runners, CPU-based inference, web servers, and high-throughput data processing workflows requiring high clock speeds and fast ephemeral storage.
